mainTopic: Searching for a קל וחומר that makes witnesses (העדאת עדים) obligate an oath: first from a person's own admission, then from a single witness
overview: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed a קל וחומר to teach that when witnesses prove part of a debt, the defendant must swear on the rest. רבה's reason for a מודה במקצת's oath is that he is only stalling. That reason does not fit a case of witnesses, so a קל וחומר is needed. The first קל וחומר learns from a person's own admission (פיו): it does not obligate a קנס, yet it obligates an oath, so witnesses, who do obligate a קנס, should surely obligate an oath. The גמרא then tests this with several ways his own mouth might be stronger than witnesses: קרבן, אשם and חומש. Each is answered by saying רבי חייא holds like רבי מאיר, who lets witnesses obligate these through a קל וחומר. But witnesses can be contradicted or proven false (הכחשה and הזמה), while a person's own admission cannot. So the proof from פיו is dropped. The גמרא tries a new קל וחומר from a single witness (עד אחד). It then starts to reject that one too, because with one witness the oath is about the very thing he testified to. This continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why a partial admitter must swear: he is only stalling
steps.stepSummary: This finishes רבה's explanation of why the Torah requires a מודה במקצת הטענה to swear. The borrower really wants to admit the whole debt but is stalling until he has money, so the Torah puts an oath on him to push him to admit everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: This borrower really wants to admit the whole debt. The reason he did not admit all of it is that he is putting the lender off. He thinks: 'Once I have money, I will pay him.' So the Torah says: put an oath on him, so that he will admit the whole thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבה's reason why someone who admits part of a debt must swear. This reason is setting up the next step: it explains why we might have thought witnesses do not create an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's idea is that a borrower does not have the nerve to deny a debt outright to his lender's face. When he admits only part, he is not truly lying about the rest. He is stalling for time, and the oath is meant to pressure him into admitting it all.

keyTerms.meaning: about all of it (the whole debt)
to evade, to put someone off
money (literally, zuz coins)
the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
put an oath on him

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה about witnesses. It is the reasoning that would have led us to think witnesses do NOT create an oath, which is exactly why the קל וחומר is needed.

phrases.english: And this one wants to admit to him about all of it.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the borrower who admitted only part of the debt. רבה is still talking here.

phrases.english: And the fact that he did not admit,
it is just that he is putting him off.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר: עַד דְּהָווּ לִי זוּזִי וּפָרַעְנָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He thinks: until I have money, and then I will pay him.
And the Merciful One said: put an oath on him
so that he will admit to him about all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's statement, which began before this section, about why a מודה במקצת swears.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מודה במקצת swears because he is only stalling, and the oath pushes him to admit the whole debt.

steps.title: Witnesses don't fit that reason, so a קל וחומר is needed
steps.stepSummary: When witnesses prove part of the debt, רבה's 'stalling' reason does not apply, so we might have said there is no oath. That is why the ברייתא teaches the oath through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when witnesses testify, you cannot use this reason, so I might say there is no oath. That is why the ברייתא teaches us the קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to why the ברייתא needed a קל וחומר: without it, we would have thought witnesses never create an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the witnesses case the defendant denied everything himself, so he is not a half-admitter who is just stalling. Since רבה's reason for the oath is missing here, we would have said no oath. The קל וחומר shows that an oath applies anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: testimony of witnesses (here, proving part of the claim)
I might say no (there is no oath)
it teaches us
a logical 'how much more so' argument

steps.whatToRemember: The קל וחומר is needed because רבה's 'he's only stalling' reason for the oath does not cover a case where witnesses prove part of the debt.

phrases.english: But testimony of witnesses,
where you cannot say this,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the stalling reason from the step before. Here he denied everything himself, so that reason doesn't fit.

phrases.english: I might say no.
It teaches us the קל וחומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הַעֲדָאַת עֵדִים, דְּלֵיכָּא לְמֵימַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 1's reasoning to the witnesses case and shows why it fails there.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קל וחומר is needed because without it, we would say witnesses do not obligate an oath, since רבה's reason does not apply to them.

steps.title: What exactly is the קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the קל וחומר works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the קל וחומר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks to spell out the קל וחומר. This sets up the next step, where it is laid out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא only said a קל וחומר exists. Now it wants the actual steps of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: and what

phrases.english: And what is the קל וחומר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the קל וחומר mentioned in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording and logic of the קל וחומר.

steps.title: If his own mouth creates an oath, surely witnesses do
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר: his own admission does not make him pay money, yet it makes him swear. Witnesses do make him pay money, so surely they make him swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his own mouth, which does not make him liable to pay money, still makes him swear, then witnesses, who do make him liable to pay money, should surely make him swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the קל וחומר: witnesses are 'stronger' than his own admission, so they should obligate an oath too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument compares two ways of proving part of a debt. It claims an admission by his own mouth is weaker because it does not create a money obligation. Witnesses do create one, so if the weaker thing brings an oath, the stronger thing surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: his mouth (his own admission)
makes him liable
money
is it not logical

phrases.english: And if his mouth, which does not make him liable for money,
phrases.notes: 'His mouth' means the defendant admitting part of the claim himself.

phrases.english: makes him liable to an oath,
witnesses, who make him liable for money,
is it not logical that they make him liable to an oath?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by giving the קל וחומר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פיו does not obligate money but obligates an oath; witnesses obligate money, so surely they obligate an oath.

steps.title: But a person's own admission does make him pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר's starting point: a person's own admission certainly makes him pay, since הודאת בעל דין is like a hundred witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does his own mouth really not make him liable for money? But a litigant's admission is like a hundred witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר by saying its first claim is simply wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'weaker' side really is weaker. But a person's own admission is as strong as a hundred witnesses, so it does obligate money. If so, witnesses are not stronger than his mouth, and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it so that (opens a challenge)
a litigant's own admission
is like a hundred witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule הודאת בעל דין כמאה עדים דמי is a basic principle all over דיני ממונות: a person's own admission is the strongest proof against him.

phrases.english: And his mouth does not make him liable for money?!
But the admission of a litigant
is like a hundred witnesses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first premise of the קל וחומר in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The premise 'פיו אין מחייבו ממון' in the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A litigant's admission is like a hundred witnesses, so it does obligate money. That means witnesses are not stronger than his mouth, and the קל וחומר breaks down.

steps.title: The 'money' means a fine, so the קל וחומר works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. The 'money' that one's own admission does not make him pay is a קנס (fine). The קל וחומר is rebuilt on that basis.
steps.simpleTranslation: What 'money' did we mean? A fine. His own mouth does not make him pay a fine, yet it makes him swear. Witnesses do make him pay a fine, so surely they make him swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the attack from step 5. When the ברייתא said 'his mouth does not make him pay money,' it meant a קנס, a fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is true that admitting a regular debt makes a person pay. But with a קנס, a person who admits it himself does not pay, while witnesses can make him pay. So witnesses really are 'stronger' than his mouth here, and the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine set by the Torah. It is a penalty, not just paying back a loss
Literally 'his mouth.' Here it means his own admission
'Is it not logical?' The closing phrase of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is taking back 'הודאת בעל דין כמאה עדים.' Admitting a regular debt still makes a person pay. Only a fine is different: if a person admits it himself, he does not pay.

phrases.english: What is the "money"? A fine.
And if his mouth, which does not make him liable for a fine,
makes him liable for an oath,
then witnesses, who do make him liable for a fine,
is it not logical that they make him liable for an oath!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by narrowing 'money' to mean a fine
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Money' meant any debt, and a person's own admission does make him pay a debt
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Money' means a קנס, which a person's own admission does not make him pay, so the קל וחומר holds

steps.title: His own mouth is stronger in one way: it can obligate a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר again. In one way a person's own mouth is stronger than witnesses: his admission makes him bring a קרבן, but witnesses do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about his mouth? It is special, because it makes him bring an offering. Can you say the same about witnesses, who do not make him bring an offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the קל וחומר. It shows a case where a person's own admission does more than witnesses do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if one side is weaker in every way. If his mouth can do something witnesses cannot do, such as obligate a קרבן, then we cannot say for sure that witnesses are 'stronger.' So we cannot learn the oath from his mouth to witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering. Here it means the חטאת brought for a sin done by mistake
'What about X? It is special because...' The standard way to break a קל וחומר
'Would you say...?' It asks if the rule really carries over to the other case

phrases.english: What about his mouth?
It is special, because it makes him liable to bring an offering.
phrases.notes: If he says, 'I did a sin by mistake,' he brings a חטאת on his own word.

phrases.english: Would you say the same about witnesses,
who do not make him liable to bring an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rebuilt קל וחומר from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from his mouth to witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In one way his mouth is stronger than witnesses (it can obligate a קרבן), so witnesses are not clearly the stronger side

steps.title: רבי חייא follows רבי מאיר: witnesses can obligate a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא holds like רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר says witnesses can obligate a קרבן, through a קל וחומר. So the challenge falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. רבי חייא holds like רבי מאיר, who says witnesses make a person bring an offering, learned from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the author of the ברייתא agrees with רבי מאיר, who holds that witnesses can obligate a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that witnesses cannot obligate a קרבן. According to רבי מאיר they can. So his mouth has no advantage over witnesses, and the קל וחומר for the oath works again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is not difficult.' It opens an answer
'He holds' (this opinion)
The תנא who taught the ברייתא with this קל וחומר
The תנא who holds that witnesses can obligate a קרבן

phrases.english: This is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: רבי חייא holds like רבי מאיר,
phrases.notes: רבי חייא is the one who taught the ברייתא with this קל וחומר.

phrases.english: who says: witnesses make him liable to bring an offering,
learned from a קל וחומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: רַבִּי חִיָּיא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the ברייתא to one side of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses cannot obligate a קרבן, so his mouth is stronger than witnesses
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי מאיר, witnesses can obligate a קרבן, and רבי חייא follows him
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברייתא's קל וחומר depends on רבי מאיר's view, not on the view of the חכמים.

steps.title: The משנה that shows רבי מאיר's view about חלב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה where רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue. Two witnesses say a person ate חלב, and he denies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: two people told him, 'You ate forbidden fat,' and he says, 'I did not eat it.' רבי מאיר says he must bring an offering, and the חכמים say he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what it just said about רבי מאיר. It is a משנה about witnesses who say a person ate חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes the person bring a קרבן based on the witnesses, even though he denies it. This proves that in רבי מאיר's view, witnesses can obligate a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As we learned in a משנה.' It introduces a source
Forbidden animal fat. Eating it by mistake requires a חטאת
Holds him liable (here, to bring a קרבן)
Hold him exempt

steps.whatToRemember: So far, by רבי מאיר's view, the קרבן challenge is answered: witnesses, like his own mouth, can obligate a קרבן. More challenges to the קל וחומר come in the next steps.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
Two people said to him: "You ate forbidden fat,"
and he says: "I did not eat it,"
רבי מאיר holds him liable, and the Sages exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי מאיר's view quoted in step 8
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds witnesses can obligate a קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כריתות: two witnesses say he ate חלב, he denies it, and רבי מאיר holds him liable

steps.title: רבי מאיר's argument and the חכמים' reply in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the quoted משנה. רבי מאיר argues that witnesses who can bring death can surely bring a קרבן. The חכמים answer that the person could just say he sinned on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: If two witnesses can bring a person to the severe punishment of death, can't they bring him to the light obligation of a קרבן? The חכמים said to him: What if he wants to say 'I did it on purpose'? Then he would be exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it began in the last step. This shows that רבי מאיר really does use a קל וחומר to make witnesses obligate a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reasons: witnesses are strong enough to cause מיתה, so they are surely strong enough to cause a קרבן. The חכמים reply that a חטאת is only brought for a sin done by accident. The person could always say he did it on purpose, so the witnesses cannot force a קרבן on him.

keyTerms.meaning: The severe punishment of death
The lighter obligation of bringing an offering
On purpose, deliberately
He would be exempt

steps.whyThisMatters: This proves the claim from step 8: according to רבי מאיר, witnesses can obligate a קרבן. So רבי חייא, who holds like רבי מאיר, is not bothered by the קרבן challenge.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
If two [witnesses] can bring him
to the severe [punishment of] death,
can they not bring him to the light [obligation of] a קרבן?
They said to him:
What if he wants to say
"I did it on purpose"? He would be exempt.
phrases.notes: A חטאת is only brought for an accidental sin, so claiming he did it on purpose gets him out of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם הֱבִיאוּהוּ שְׁנַיִם לִידֵי מִיתָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי מאיר, witnesses can obligate a קרבן through a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about two witnesses who say a person ate חלב (כריתות).

steps.title: A person's own mouth obligates an אשם
steps.stepSummary: A new attack: a person's own admission obligates him to bring an אשם, but witnesses do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is what is special about his own mouth: it obligates him to bring an אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new way to show that a person's own admission is stronger than witnesses. If that is true, the קל וחומר breaks down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's קל וחומר needs a person's own mouth to be weaker than witnesses in every way. Here the גמרא points to an אשם, which comes through his own admission. If witnesses cannot bring an אשם, then his mouth has an advantage.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; here it introduces a new attempt at a challenge
What about his mouth? (meaning: his mouth has a special strength)
A guilt-offering

phrases.english: Rather: what about his mouth?
For it obligates him [to bring] an אשם!
phrases.notes: This is the אשם of someone who wrongly kept another person's money and then admits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָה לְפִיו – שֶׁכֵּן מְחַיְּיבוֹ אָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קרבן challenge was answered, the גמרא tries a different strength of a person's own mouth.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's קל וחומר from a person's own admission to witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a person's own mouth obligates an אשם and witnesses do not, then his mouth is not weaker in every way.

steps.title: An אשם is just a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an אשם is a type of קרבן, so the answer already given for קרבן covers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אשם is the same as a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the אשם challenge in a few words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw that רבי מאיר makes witnesses obligate a קרבן through a קל וחומר. An אשם is just one kind of קרבן, so the same answer works. Witnesses can obligate it too, according to רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

phrases.english: An אשם is the same as a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אשם challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Folds the new case into an earlier answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An אשם is a separate strength of a person's own mouth.
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשם is a type of קרבן, and רבי מאיר already lets witnesses obligate a קרבן.

steps.title: A person's own mouth obligates a חומש
steps.stepSummary: Another attack: a person's own admission obligates him to add an extra fifth, but witnesses do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is what is special about his own mouth: it obligates him to pay an extra fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries yet another strength of a person's own admission, this time a payment instead of a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חומש is an extra fifth added when someone returns money he wrongly kept, after admitting it. This is not a קרבן, so the last answer may not cover it. If witnesses cannot obligate a חומש, his mouth is stronger here.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra fifth added to a payment
Obligates him

phrases.english: Rather: what about his mouth?
For it obligates him [to pay] a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָה לְפִיו – שֶׁכֵּן מְחַיְּיבוֹ חוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the אשם challenge failed, the גמרא tries the חומש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חומש is not a קרבן, so the רבי מאיר answer may not apply. If only his own mouth obligates it, his mouth is stronger than witnesses.

steps.title: רבי מאיר would apply the קל וחומר to חומש too
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי חייא holds like רבי מאיר, the same קל וחומר that makes witnesses obligate a קרבן also makes them obligate a חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. רבי חייא holds like רבי מאיר. Just as רבי מאיר obligates a קרבן through a קל וחומר, he also obligates a חומש through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the חומש challenge using the same idea it used for קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reasoning was: witnesses can do the most severe thing (cause death), so they can surely do lighter things. That logic works just as well for a חומש. So according to רבי מאיר, witnesses can obligate a חומש too, and a person's own mouth has no advantage here.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
He holds (this opinion)
Just as

phrases.english: This is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: רבי חייא holds like רבי מאיר.
Just as he obligates him
[to bring] a קרבן from a קל וחומר,
he obligates him [to pay] a fifth from a קל וחומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, רַבִּי חִיָּיא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חומש challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends an earlier answer to a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a person's own admission obligates a חומש.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, the same קל וחומר lets witnesses obligate a חומש.

steps.title: A person's own mouth cannot be contradicted or proven false
steps.stepSummary: A new and stronger attack: witnesses can be contradicted (הכחשה) or proven false (הזמה), but a person's own admission cannot. So his mouth is stronger in this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is what is special about his own mouth: it cannot be contradicted or proven false by הזמה. Would you say the same about witnesses, who can be contradicted and can be proven false by הזמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more strength of a person's own admission, one that has nothing to do with קרבנות or payments. No answer is given: the גמרא accepts this challenge, and in the next step it drops the proof from his mouth and tries a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge is about how reliable the evidence is, not about what it can obligate. Other witnesses can cancel what witnesses say, but nothing cancels a person's own admission. רבי מאיר's view does not help here, so the גמרא accepts the objection and gives up learning from פיו.

keyTerms.meaning: Contradiction: other witnesses deny the event itself
Proving witnesses false by showing they were somewhere else at the time
Would you say (the same)?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הכחשה and הזמה. In הכחשה the new witnesses argue about what happened. In הזמה they say the first witnesses were with them somewhere else, so they could not have seen it.

phrases.english: Rather: what about his mouth?
For it is not subject to contradiction or to הזמה.
Would you say [the same] about witnesses,
who are subject to contradiction and to הזמה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָה לְפִיו – שֶׁכֵּן אֵינוֹ בְּהַכְחָשָׁה וּבַהֲזָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the חומש challenge failed, the גמרא brings a strength that רבי מאיר's קל וחומר cannot answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's קל וחומר from a person's own admission to witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person's own admission can never be cancelled, but witnesses can. So his mouth is stronger, and you cannot reason from his mouth to witnesses.

steps.title: Deriving the oath from a single witness instead
steps.stepSummary: Since the קל וחומר from פיו failed, the גמרא builds a new קל וחומר from עד אחד: if one witness, who cannot obligate money, obligates a שבועה, then two witnesses, who do obligate money, should surely obligate a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from one witness. If one witness, who does not make him pay money, makes him swear an oath, then witnesses, who do make him pay money, surely make him swear an oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old source (a person's own admission) and offers a new source for רבי חייא's rule: the law of עד אחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One witness is weaker than two, because he cannot make anyone pay. Even so, the Torah says his testimony forces the defendant to swear. So two witnesses, who are strong enough to make him pay, should certainly be strong enough to force an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, meaning it is learned from
A single witness
Money, meaning an obligation to pay
An oath
Is it not logical? This is the classic wording that closes a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the earlier קל וחומר with new wording. The starting point has changed completely: before, it was a person's own admission (פיו). Now it is a single witness.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes from one witness:
phrases.notes: "It" means רבי חייא's rule that witnesses can obligate an oath.

phrases.english: And if one witness
who does not obligate him to pay money,
obligates him to take an oath,
then witnesses, who obligate him to pay money,
is it not logical that they obligate him to take an oath!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 knocked out the קל וחומר from פיו, this step replaces it with a new קל וחומר from עד אחד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the source: a new base for the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא's rule rested on a קל וחומר from a person's own admission, which was just refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule can instead rest on a קל וחומר from עד אחד, who obligates an oath even though he cannot obligate money.

steps.title: A single witness has a special feature
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the new קל וחומר: one witness is special, because the defendant swears about the very thing the witness testified about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about one witness? That the defendant swears about the very thing the witness testifies about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the proof from עד אחד by pointing out something special about it. The comparison continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one witness, the defendant swears about the very thing the witness testified to, so the oath answers his testimony directly. In רבי חייא's case of two witnesses, they proved one part of the debt and he must swear about the other part, which they never testified about. So the קל וחומר does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: What about this case? It is special in that... This is the standard wording for breaking a קל וחומר.
Testifies
Swears an oath

phrases.english: What is special about one witness?
That about what he testifies,
he swears,
phrases.notes: "He" here is the defendant, who swears about the exact thing the witness said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new קל וחומר from step 16 by showing that its source, עד אחד, has a special feature.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from עד אחד to two witnesses
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With one witness, the oath is about the very matter he testified about. In העדאת עדים, the oath is about the rest of the claim, which the witnesses did not testify about, so the comparison breaks.
